scenes.text: Imagine you buy a laptop, and it breaks. You say the warranty covers it. The business says it does not. Today, the rules live inside the business's own process, and the person who decides is often on their side. LGtie is built to fix that.

Here is how it works. The business publishes its rules first, as simple yes or no questions. This is a real warranty policy, running as a small circuit on X Layer through TapeOut, so nobody can quietly change it. Tap an answer, and the result and the reason change. Anyone can check it, for free.

When there is a dispute, both sides answer the same questions. Where their answers match, it is settled. Only the questions they disagree on go to a neutral reviewer, someone both sides agreed to in advance. This is a real case on X Layer. Six answers matched, and one did not, so only that one went to the reviewer. The result is covered. Now, the receipt. It shows who said what, who settled each question, and the rules, re-run live. I ran this case myself, so it is a demonstration, not a customer.

Customers do not need a crypto wallet. This is a customer's page. They answer the questions, and approve with the fingerprint or face scan that unlocks their phone. Now, the business's inbox. The customer's signed answers are waiting here, and one click submits them. Evidence works the same way. The customer picks a photo, or writes a note, and only a fingerprint of it is recorded. Nothing is uploaded. And a business that wants no clicking at all can run an optional helper, that sends a message to Slack, and submits for it.

The neutral reviewer sees side A and side B, instead of names. They answer the disputed question, and have to write down their reasons. Those reasons are shown on the case, and on the receipt, where both sides can read them. That makes a bad decision visible. It cannot stop one.
Who is it for? Businesses that handle warranty claims, refunds, or bug bounties. The proposed model is a small fee for each reviewed decision, or for a permanent receipt.

LGtie cannot tell whether an answer is true, and a reviewer can still be wrong. What it does is make the rules clear, so anyone can re-check the result. It is live on X Layer today. Thanks for watching.
